introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

figures.legende: Inequality diagram: lines y = x and x + y = 12 drawn on axes (x up to 14, y up to 14); hatching marks the rejected side of each line and of the x-axis, leaving the triangle with vertices (0,0), (12,0) and (6,6) unshaded.

incertitudes: Q5(i) : sur le schema, les hachures de y = x sont au-dessus de la droite, celles de x + y = 12 au-dessus et a droite, celles de l'axe des x en dessous ; la region non hachuree est donc le triangle (0,0), (12,0), (6,6). Les trois inequations retenues sont y >= 0, y <= x et x + y <= 12.

Q5(i)(b) : l'enonce imprime est confus (« If he must sell both ... »). Lecture retenue : cout = 125x + 50y avec x et y tels que l'homme vende des deux produits (x >= 1, y >= 1, nombres entiers de tasses) ; maximum 1425 francs en (11, 1). Si l'on evalue seulement les sommets du triangle, on obtient 1500 francs en (12, 0), point ou aucune tasse de mais n'est vendue : les deux resultats sont donnes dans le corrige. Le bareme officiel attend sans doute l'un des deux : a trancher par un relecteur.

Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks » ; total 66 + 17 + 17 = 100).
Le sujet est une photo numerisee (CamScanner) : texte lu en image page par page ; les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ont ete ignores.

questions.enonce_markdown:
5. (i) A man sells $x$ cups of patched groundnuts and $y$ cups of patched corn during break in a certain school as shown in the inequality diagram below.

![fig-1](gce-ol-additional-maths-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_1.png)

From the diagram,

a) write down three inequalities in terms of $x$ and $y$ that satisfy the unshaded region. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each line has hatching on the side that is **rejected**; the unshaded region is the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(12,0)$ and $(6,6)$.

- Line $y=x$ (hatched above it): the region lies on or below the line, so $y\le x$. Test: $(6,0)$ is unshaded and $0\le6$.
- Line $x+y=12$ (it passes through $(12,0)$ and $(0,12)$; hatched above and to the right): the region lies on or below it, so $x+y\le12$. Test: $(1,0)$ gives $1\le12$.
- The $x$-axis is hatched below: the region lies on or above it, so $y\ge0$.

(As the man must sell both products, $y>0$ and $x>0$ in practice.)

**Answer: $y\ge0$, $\;y\le x$, $\;x+y\le12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) If he must sell both patched groundnuts and patched corn, and a cup of patched groundnuts costs $125$ francs and a cup of patched corn costs $50$ francs, find the maximum expenditure that can be incurred by the man. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The expenditure is $C=125x+50y$ (in francs). The values of $x$ and $y$ are numbers of cups, so they are whole numbers, and he sells both products, so $x\ge1$ and $y\ge1$.

**Vertices of the region.** $(0,0)$, $(12,0)$ and $(6,6)$ (the intersection of $y=x$ and $x+y=12$).

| Vertex | $C=125x+50y$ |
|---|---|
| $(0,0)$ | $0$ |
| $(12,0)$ | $1500$ |
| $(6,6)$ | $1050$ |

The largest value on the triangle is at $(12,0)$, but there he sells **no corn** ($y=0$), which is not allowed. Along the line $x+y=12$ we have $C=125x+50(12-x)=600+75x$, which is largest when $x$ is largest, so the best allowed point is $x=11$, $y=1$ (it satisfies $y\le x$ and $x+y=12$):

$$C=125(11)+50(1)=1375+50=1425.$$

(Check: $x=10,y=2$ gives $1350$, smaller.)

**Answer: maximum expenditure $=1425$ francs** (11 cups of groundnuts and 1 cup of corn). If the point $(12,0)$ were allowed, the vertex method would give $1500$ francs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) The points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(-2,5)$ and $(3,-1)$ respectively. Find

a) the gradient of the straight line $AB$. *[2 marks]*
(ii)(b) the equation of the straight line joining the points $A$ and $B$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ with $A(-2,5)$ and $m=-\dfrac65$:

$$y-5=-\frac65(x+2).$$

Multiply by $5$: $5y-25=-6x-12$, so $6x+5y=13$.

Check with $B(3,-1)$: $6(3)+5(-1)=18-5=13$.

**Answer: $6x+5y=13$** (equivalently $y=-\dfrac65x+\dfrac{13}5$).
